chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

I asked my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who entered [Mecca] before Tarwiyah by a day and intended to enter the state of Ihram for Hajj, but made a mistake and said 'Umrah. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him, let him renew the Ihram for Hajj.' And it is not permissible for one who has entered Ihram for Hajj to perform Tawaf of the House as a voluntary act until he returns from Mina. If he did that out of forgetfulness, there is no penalty upon him. Narrated.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina
key_terms.الْإِحْرَامَ: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim mistakenly performs Umrah Ihram instead of Hajj Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies the flexibility in changing one's Hajj intention before the 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, emphasizing that a simple renewal of Ihram suffices without penalty for the error. It further establishes the jurisprudential principle that voluntary acts, such as Tawaf al-Ada or Tawaf al-Nafila, are suspended during the specific phase of Hajj until the pilgrim returns from Mina, reflecting the distinct ritual status of the Hajj pilgrim. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on ease (yusr) in ritual obligations, distinguishing between intentional deviation and accidental mistake.
